customer-jane: We're seeing 502 / TLS handshake failures when calling our API through the interface endpoint from our VPC. Other endpoints (health, embeddings) work fine. Any ideas?
sophia: Can you paste a curl run from an instance inside the same subnet? :thinking:
matt: Also which region and endpoint type (interface vs gateway)?
customer-jane: Interface endpoint in us-east-1. From our bastion: 
```
> dig api.redwood.internal +short
10.0.5.12
> curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
* Connected to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```
matt: That curl error usually means TLS inspection / MITM or SNI mismatch. Can you run openssl s_client to see the cert? Use -servername to set SNI.

```
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -alpn h2
```

sophia: Also please paste `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-id vpc-xxxxx` output (mask IDs) so we can confirm the endpoint network interfaces.

customer-jane: openssl output below (sanitized):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = *.redwood-hosted.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.2
    Cipher    : ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
    Session-ID: ...
    Verification: OK
```

tao: Interesting — cert CN is `*.redwood-hosted.com`. That suggests the server presented our default hosted cert. If your client expects `api.redwood.internal` in SAN it will fail unless SNI/Host header align. But typically we support the hosted hostname via SNI. Can you try forcing SNI/Host to the external host we expect?

```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H "Host: api.redwood-hosted.com"
```

matt: Also check whether your corporate proxy is doing TLS interception. Those proxies will present their own cert, or strip SNI/ALPN which can cause TLS version/cipher differences and handshake failures. Any egress proxies?

customer-jane: We tested bypassing our proxy for that host and the call succeeded. So when we go through proxy we get the failure.

sophia: OK that points at outbound TLS inspection. Two remediation options: add api.redwood.internal (or the hosted domain) to the proxy bypass/allowlist, or deploy the proxy with the redwood CA chain installed (not recommended unless you fully trust). If you must keep inspection, ensure the proxy preserves SNI and ALPN h2.

matt: Additional things to verify while you're here:
- Make sure the endpoint network interfaces are in the same AZ/subnet and SGs allow TCP 443 from your client IPs. We need ephemeral ports open back to the client (1024-65535) for the connection to establish.
- Confirm Route 53 private hosted zone isn't rewriting the record to a public IP. `dig +short api.redwood.internal` should return the interface ENI private IPs.
- If you use an HTTP CONNECT proxy, confirm it allows CONNECT to the host:port without tampering.

customer-jane: We ran tcpdump while hitting the endpoint via proxy and saw the proxy re-terminating TLS and not forwarding SNI. When we bypassed the proxy the TLS handshake negotiated h2 and the request completed.

tao: Good find. For KB: common failure modes are (1) corporate TLS inspection altering cert/SNI, (2) DNS split-horizon misconfig mapping to wrong IP, (3) security group or NACL blocking ephemeral ports, (4) endpoint policy denying the principal.

customer-jane: Quick checklist we followed that fixed it: 
1) Verified `dig` returns ENI private IPs, not public.
2) Ran `openssl s_client -connect <eni-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -alpn h2` to inspect certificate and ALPN.
3) Confirmed corporate proxy was doing TLS inspection; added `api.redwood.internal` to proxy bypass.
4) Confirmed SGs allow inbound from our subnets and ephemeral ports.
5) Retried and got 200s.

sophia: I'll add a KB article with the repro steps and recommended proxy-bypass snippet for common proxy appliances (Bluecoat, ZScaler, Palo Alto). Also will note to check ALPN/h2 requirement. :memo:

helpdesk-bot: Follow-up ticket created: INC-7890. Assigned to oncall infra.

customer-jane: Thanks everyone — workaround applied and customer confirmed success. :tada:
